source_text: Quae postremo palma tolerantiae, si dolor vulnerum et verberum, intercepto itinere sensuum, pertingere ad animum non valebat? Quo ergo profecit Apollinaris adulatio? Videlicet ut omnis virtutum pulchritudo, quam in se Christus expresserat, indebitis naturae eius laudibus vacuata flaccesceret, cunctoque veritatis suae splendore nudata sacrum magisterium Mediatoris offerret irrisui. Huc accedebat quoniam non solum operum suorum perdebat insignia, nativitate, non virtute felicior; sed etiam fraudis criminibus urgebatur, si indiceret mortalibus: Extendimini ad patientiam hominis nihil sentientis, et venite per veras cruces ad virtutes corporis falsi nihil dolentis; vel: Imitamini castitatem, certa naturae vestrae irritamenta vincentes, illius quem debilitas fecit pudicum videri. Certe nihil profanius, nihil scelestius talibus excogitari commentis potest. Et Apollinaris omnia ista non dixerat; per illud unum quod pronuntiarat, homini Christo defuisse eos sensus, qui a natura inditi, non usu, sed excessu ad vitia labuntur; haec omnia quae a Catholicis relata sunt, praeiudicio opinionis suae mutus excepit. Horum quippe cunctorum affirmatione construitur catholica fides, quorum negatione vel consecutione Apollinaris haeresis compacta est atque damnata. Tu igitur conice quid de te debeat iudicari, qui commixtionem sexuum damnas, ut Manichaeus; naturam carnis Christi a communione hominum sequestras, secundum Manichaeos; concupiscentiam carnis accusas, iuxta praeceptoris tui dicta Manichaei; dicis concupiscentiam sensuum in Christi corpore non fuisse, vel secundum Manichaeos vel secundum Apollinaristas; et tamen vis a nobis nec Apollinarista, nec Manichaeus vocari. Quamquam do manus, praestoque beneficium; nec nos liberalitatis poenitet; per me ut Apollinaris sectator non videaris licebit; minoris quippe est ille impietatis inventor; per te autem non licet ut voceris aliud quam Manichaeus.
pass_a_gloss: Finally what palm of endurance, if the pain of wounds and of blows, the path of the senses having been intercepted, was not able to reach the mind? To what therefore did Apollinaris's flattery profit? Namely that all the beauty of virtues which Christ had expressed in himself would droop, emptied by praises not owed to his nature, and, stripped of all the splendor of its truth, would offer the sacred teaching of the Mediator to mockery. To this it was added that he was not only losing the insignia of his works, luckier by nativity than by virtue; but was also being pressed by charges of fraud, if he declared to mortals: Stretch yourselves to the patience of a human being feeling nothing, and come through true crosses to the virtues of a false body feeling no pain; or: Imitate chastity, conquering the sure irritants of your nature, of him whom weakness made seem modest. Certainly nothing more profane, nothing more wicked can be thought out by such inventions. And Apollinaris had not said all those things; through that one thing which he had pronounced, that those senses were lacking to the human Christ, which put in by nature slide to vices not by use but by excess; he received mute all these things which were reported by the Catholics by the prior judgment of his opinion. For by the affirmation of all these the catholic faith is constructed, by whose negation or following the heresy of Apollinaris was compacted and condemned. You therefore gather what ought to be judged about you, who condemn the mingling of the sexes, as Manichaeus; sequester the nature of Christ's flesh from the communion of humans, according to the Manichaeans; accuse the desire of the flesh, according to the sayings of your teacher Manichaeus; say that the desire of the senses was not in Christ's body, either according to the Manichaeans or according to the Apollinarists; and nevertheless you want to be called by us neither Apollinarist nor Manichaean. Although I give my hands, and furnish a benefit; nor does generosity repent us; through me it will be allowed that you not seem a follower of Apollinaris; for he is the inventor of a lesser impiety; but through you it is not allowed that you be called anything other than Manichaean.

Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: Finally, what prize was there for endurance if the pain of wounds and blows could not reach the soul because the path of sensation was blocked? What, then, did Apollinaris’s flattery achieve? All the beauty of the virtues Christ had embodied was emptied out and withered by undeserved praises of his nature. Stripped of all the splendor of its truth, it exposed the Mediator’s sacred teaching to ridicule. Moreover, he would not merely lose the distinction of his works, being fortunate by birth rather than by virtue: he would also face charges of fraud if he told mortals, “Strive toward the patience of a man who feels nothing, and come through real torments to the virtues of an unreal body that suffers no pain”; or, “Conquer the definite impulses of your own nature and imitate the chastity of someone whom weakness made appear pure.” Certainly nothing more profane or wicked can be imagined than such inventions.

Apollinaris had not actually said all these things. But by making that one pronouncement—that the man Christ lacked the sensations implanted by nature, which fall into vice through excess rather than through use—he received all these replies from the catholics in silence, condemned by his own opinion. For the catholic faith is built by affirming all the things whose denial, or the consequences of whose denial, formed and condemned Apollinaris’s heresy. Judge, then, what verdict should be passed on you. You condemn the union of the sexes like Manichaeus. You separate the nature of Christ’s flesh from the common condition of humanity, according to the Manichaeans. You accuse the desire of the flesh, following the statements of your teacher Manichaeus. You say that sensory desire was not present in Christ’s body, whether according to the Manichaeans or according to the Apollinarists. Yet you want us to call you neither an Apollinarist nor a Manichaean! Still, I yield and grant you a favor; I do not regret being generous. As far as I am concerned, you may avoid appearing a follower of Apollinaris, for he devised the lesser impiety. But you yourself make it impossible for you to be called anything other than a Manichaean.

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Julian defends marital union (commixtio) as God's work, not the devil's property.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
